chunks: "It was named al-ʿAtīq because it is a house set free from people, and no one has ever owned it."

key_terms.الْعَتِيقَ: al-ʿAtīq; the ancient or emancipated one, a name of the Ka'bah
key_terms.بَيْتٌ: a house; referring here to the Sacred House
key_terms.عَتِيقٌ: ancient, noble, or free from possession
key_terms.مِنَ النَّاسِ: from the people; independent of human claim or ownership

ai.seo_question: Why is the Ka'bah called al-ʿAtīq in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report explains why the Ka'bah is called al-ʿAtīq. It states that it is a noble, ancient house detached from human ownership, belonging to none among the people.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "It was named al-Atiq (the Ancient) because it is a house independent of people and has never been owned by anyone."
